memories_potentially_to_write: When the project has a `test-support`-style feature pattern (or similar workspace convention), check it BEFORE dispatching a worker so the worker doesn't reintroduce known-bad inline helpers. Memory candidate: `feedback_check_workspace_test_support_pattern`.
key_lessons: Reviewers enforce the LITERAL text of `[hard]` criteria — paraphrased dispatch prompts override the criterion; if the worker complies with the paraphrase, the reviewer will fail it. Memory `feedback_quote_jit_criteria_verbatim` already covers this but the StdRng vs Lcg case shows it again.
Lead's pre-dispatch criterion audit must check the existing workspace conventions (gf2-core's `test-support` feature) — would have caught the SSOT duplication BEFORE T10 + T11 were dispatched.

Lead-direct fixes are still cheap when the rework is mechanical and the dispatched workers don't have memory of the cross-issue fix. Don't redispatch for cosmetic / structural refactors that are 50 LOC and trivially verifiable.
